children: Oracle (ORCL, Financials) is facing increased pressure in the credit market as the cost of insuring its debt jumped to a record high on fears about the huge tab for its AI expansion.

The yield on Oracle's 6.7% bonds due 2056 climbed above 8% for the first time on Thursday, according to Seeking Alpha statistics. That is a big move for a company that is rated Baa2 by Moody's and BBB- by S&P, near the bottom of investment grade.

The pressure comes as Oracle spends money on the data centers and processing resources needed to compete in artificial intelligence. That development has made the company more reliant on debt financing, making borrowing rates a key aspect of the investing story.
Shares of Oracle fell approximately 4% Thursday afternoon to around $139.

Adding to the uncertainty, Oracle is said to have sent a force majeure notice to the developer of its Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico. The action is meant to safeguard Oracle from some financial exposure if regulatory and infrastructure challenges delay the planned inauguration of the facility in 2028.

Oracle is not the only one. Credit default swaps have also widened on a few of big tech names as investors rethink the cost of the industry's AI infrastructure expansion. Adding to the burden are rising Treasury yields, which are making borrowing more expensive across the market.
The next catalyst for Oracle will be whether its growing AI cloud business can produce enough growth and cash flow to match the investments needed to construct it.

title: Oracle's AI Bet Just Sent a Warning Signal to Credit Markets
